original.target_description: Relationship between individual video-based police firearms training and senior police officers’ tactical gaze control and visual attention. Supplied locator: p. 10. Multiple outcome/model-term candidates remain unresolved.

n.exclusions: Outcome-specific exclusions documented in section 3.1; retained as candidates in notes.

replication.target_description: Unassigned replication side; no replication source inspected in this source-grouped task.

notes:
Identity verified independently from canonical text: Frontiers ORIGINAL RESEARCH article, 24 April 2024; title When failure is not an option: a police firearms training concept for improving decision-making in shoot/don’t shoot scenarios; Joshua Olma, Christine Sutter, Sandra Sülzenbrück; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2024.1335892. Supplied text contains full primary-report sections 1–5, participant methods, results, tables and discussion, rather than only an abstract. No PDF was supplied, so printed page boundaries cannot be independently inspected or rendered.
The description identifies the broad training relationship and senior-officer sample but does not specify the dependent variable, model term (Time, Group, or interaction), pre/post exploratory comparison, or group-specific contrast. Multiple primary tests fit. Page-only locators in an unpaginated HTML parse do not uniquely identify a test. No assignments are made from audit_id, row order, requested metric, or numeric agreement. All positive values remain unassigned candidates; analytic n is also unresolved because outcome/model and group-specific analysis determine the participant subset. No N is derived from df and no metric is converted. Printed candidates include inequalities such as partial eta squared <0.01 and p<0.001, retained literally in the quoted blocks. Even where the authors call p<.05 main effects non-significant, printed p values are preserved without reinterpretation.
Only original unfinished fields are assigned; replication and reported_success are placeholders.
